solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cryptic method, so clue giving little away (5-7)

indicatorNotes.Cryptic: something cryptic is scrambled out of plain sense, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A remark on how a cryptic clue works: its method is to reveal as little as possible.
annotation.walkthrough: The self-referential surface makes 'Cryptic' look like a description of the puzzle rather than an instruction, and 'so' looks like a link word when it is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a reticent person keeps secrets rather than letting them slip.

entries.clue: Something you do to feed after due date? (7)

annotation.definition: Something you do to feed after due date

indicatorNotes.to feed: one piece is fed into another, going inside it

blocks.note: late = after the due date
an act is something you do; these letters go inside the other piece

annotation.surface: A riddle about something a new mother does once the baby, overdue or not, has arrived.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight it defines the answer (a mother lactates to feed her baby after the due date), and read piece by piece it builds L-ACT-ATE.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: producing milk is what a mother does to nourish a baby born after its due date.

entries.clue: Trapped by falls, start to swim then leap (9)

indicatorNotes.start to: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of swim
in storytelling, 'now' means at that time, as in 'now he was angry'
a bound is a leap

annotation.surface: A swimmer caught under waterfalls, trying to swim clear and then leap away.
annotation.walkthrough: The falls of the surface are waterfalls; in the definition they are snowfalls.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic twist on a plain sense: the falls are of snow, which can leave people unable to leave home.

entries.clue: Low note, fiver perhaps (6)

annotation.definitionNote: a fiver is one example of money

blocks.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
lah is a note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A little musical or monetary pun: a low note, a banknote worth five pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low note' reads as a deep sound, and a fiver (a five-pound note) seems to continue that; 'low' is actually the cow's verb. 'Perhaps' flags the fiver as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a five-pound note is one instance of cash, for which the answer is slang.

entries.clue: Easy to see runs wanted for hundred in ground (8)

indicatorNotes.wanted: wanted means lacking, so the runs are taken out
indicatorNotes.ground: ground grain is broken up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken literally
R = runs, the cricket abbreviation; removed, leaving HUNDEDIN to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A cricket scene: a batsman needs runs to reach a hundred on the ground, in plain view.
annotation.walkthrough: Cricket words, runs, hundred and ground, hide that 'hundred' is only letters and 'ground' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something not concealed is in plain view.

entries.clue: Secondary schools that boy’s going round superficially goodish (5)

indicatorNotes.superficially: only the surface of the word, its outside letters, is used

blocks.note: his = belonging to that boy
the outer letters of goodish, which go inside HIS

annotation.surface: A parent's verdict that a son's secondary schooling is only superficially goodish.
annotation.walkthrough: A high, short for high school, is the American name for a secondary school.
annotation.definitionFit: An American usage: the word is short for high school, the US name for the upper years of schooling.

entries.clue: Soldier bore with American thug sharing a cell (7)

indicatorNotes.sharing a cell: the two words share one square of the grid, overlapping by a letter

blocks.note: a drag is a bore; its final G is shared with the next piece
goon is American slang for a hired thug

annotation.surface: A soldier locked up with a dull cellmate and an American heavy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sharing a cell' paints a prison, but here the cell is a grid square: DRAG and GOON overlap on the G.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: dragoons were originally mounted infantry, and the name survives in some cavalry regiments.

entries.clue: Maybe open expensive wines, taking one aboard for Agnes (12)

annotation.definitionNote: the Open is one example of a championship

indicatorNotes.taking: the wines take in new letters
indicatorNotes.for: the new letters stand in for AGNES

blocks.note: champagnes are costly wines
AGNES is removed from the end of CHAMPAGNES, leaving CHAMP
I = one, the Roman numeral
on ship = aboard

annotation.surface: Someone opening pricey wine for a guest called Agnes, one more joining the party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Open' sounds like uncorking the wine, but it is the golf tournament. Agnes is not a person: the letters AGNES sit at the end of CHAMPAGNES and get swapped out.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by 'Maybe': the Open is golf's oldest major tournament.

entries.clue: High pipe still cold and loo out of order (7)

indicatorNotes.out of order: the letters are not in their proper order, so rearrange them

blocks.note: a still (photograph) is a pic
C = cold, as on a tap
rearranged

annotation.surface: A complaint that a pipe is still cold and the toilet is broken: plumbing woes.
annotation.walkthrough: The plumbing picture makes 'pipe' a water pipe, but it is a musical one; 'loo' is British for toilet, and 'out of order' puts its letters out of order.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: this small flute sounds an octave above the ordinary one, the highest pipe in the orchestra.

entries.clue: Upright piano slipped, tuner maybe coming after dinner? (12)

blocks.note: a post is an upright
p = piano, quietly in music
slipped away = ran off
a radio's tuner is a dial

annotation.surface: An upright piano slides, and the piano tuner turns up after dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upright piano' and 'tuner' belong together in the surface, but every word is a separate piece. 'Piano' is the musical instruction for soft, abbreviated P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Latin: post = after, prandium = a meal, as in a nap following a meal.

entries.clue: Pants take up entire laundry (7)

blocks.note: to hog something is to take all of it
the wash = the laundry

annotation.surface: Trousers filling a whole load of washing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British slang for rubbish or nonsense, as in 'that film was pants', not trousers or underwear.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in British slang 'pants' means rubbish or nonsense, and so does the answer.

entries.clue: Big shot reportedly put hole in ship’s side (9)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: a report is heard, so go by the sound

blocks.note: a big shot is a star
bored = drilled a hole in

annotation.surface: A news item: a celebrity allegedly drilled a hole in the side of a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big shot' suggests gunfire holing a ship, but it is an important person.
annotation.definitionFit: A nautical term: the right-hand side of a vessel as you face the bow.

entries.clue: Rush to seize protestor munching sandwiches (5)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the words hold the answer between them like bread round a filling

blocks.note: spans the end of protestor and the first letter of munching

annotation.surface: A protester eating sandwiches as the crowd rushes to take a building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Munching sandwiches' is one picture, but 'munching' is fodder and 'sandwiches' the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A military sense: to take a place by a sudden violent assault.

entries.clue: Where riders may be introduced by heartless groom? (6)

annotation.definition: Where riders may be introduced by heartless groom

indicatorNotes.heartless: the middle letter is taken out

blocks.note: PREEN = groom, minus its central E
in racing a jockey who is riding is 'up', as in 'Dettori up'

annotation.surface: An unromantic bridegroom adding extra clauses to the marriage contract.
annotation.walkthrough: Riders are added clauses in a contract as well as jockeys. The whole clue defines the answer, and it also builds it, with the pieces taken in reverse clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a cold-hearted groom might add riders, extra clauses, to a prenuptial agreement.

entries.clue: Drop into New Delhi bar opening in capital (8)

indicatorNotes.into: one piece goes into the other
indicatorNotes.New: the letters are made new, rearranged
indicatorNotes.bar opening: bar means except, so leave off the opening letter

blocks.note: DELHI minus its first letter D, then rearranged
to drop is to sink; these letters go inside the other piece

annotation.surface: Someone dropping into a bar in New Delhi, the Indian capital.
annotation.walkthrough: New Delhi is a capital, so it tempts as the definition; but 'New' is the anagram signal and the capital meant is in Finland.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the city is Finland's seat of government.

entries.clue: Van at this point drove too fast for Spooner (9)

indicatorNotes.for Spooner: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: here = at this point; takes the SP sound from the other word
sped = went too fast; takes the H sound from the other word

annotation.surface: A van driver speeding at this spot, as told to the famously muddled Reverend Spooner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Van' looks like a vehicle, to go with the speeding, but it is short for vanguard, the front of an army.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: van, short for vanguard, is the leading part of an army or movement.

entries.clue: Painter perhaps made an entrance out of sight (2,6)

blocks.note: came in, written in the storytelling order 'in came'
RA = Royal Academician, an artist

annotation.surface: A painter arrives, then slips out of view.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'Painter made an entrance' as 'in came RA', like 'in came the doctor'.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal Latin idiom: proceedings held privately, closed to the public's view.

entries.clue: Chance I had to open Molière’s grave? (8)

indicatorNotes.to open: the letters are placed into the other word, opening it up

blocks.note: the grave is a French accent, as Molière would use
I'd = I had; these letters go inside the accent

annotation.surface: A gravedigger's chance discovery: by luck I got to open Molière's tomb.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grave' is not a tomb but the grave accent, the backward-sloping mark on French letters such as è in Molière itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an unplanned event, as in meeting by luck.

entries.clue: King checks and changes roll of film (7)

blocks.note: CR = Carolus Rex, King Charles in Latin, as on a royal cypher
to edit is to check and change a text

annotation.surface: A monarch inspecting and altering a roll of photographic film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roll of film' suggests a camera spool; here it is the list of names that rolls at the end of a movie.
annotation.definitionFit: A film-industry sense: the list of cast and crew scrolls up the screen at the end of a movie.

entries.clue: Act as a prisoner’s guiding light (6)

blocks.note: to act as is to be
taken as written
con = convict

annotation.surface: An inmate who becomes a guiding light to fellow prisoners.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive in the surface; in the wordplay it stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a signal fire or lamp set up to show the way to ships or travellers.

entries.clue: New French designer clothes, medium (7)

indicatorNotes.clothes: as a verb, the designer clothes the letter, surrounding it

blocks.note: Coco Chanel, French fashion designer
N = new; goes inside the designer's name

annotation.surface: A fashion note about new clothes from a French designer, sized medium.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as the noun for garments; it is the verb, dressing N in CHANEL. 'Medium' is not a size but a means of communication.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a means by which something is communicated, such as television or the press.

entries.clue: Plaster didn’t come off, I’m surprised to hear (6)

indicatorNotes.to hear: the pieces are to be heard, not spelt

blocks.note: stuck = didn't come off; oh = I'm surprised

annotation.surface: Someone surprised that a plaster stayed stuck on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface plaster is a sticking plaster, a bandage; the answer is the plaster on walls.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a fine plaster used to coat walls and mould decoration.

entries.clue: Shift for one female prison officer without conflict (5)

indicatorNotes.without: the second piece is left out of the first

blocks.note: a wardress is a female prison warder
WAR = conflict, removed from the front

annotation.surface: A work shift for a woman prison officer that passes without trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shift' reads as a work shift to match the prison officer; it is a loose, straight frock, and 'for one' marks it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by 'for one': a shift is a straight, loose-fitting frock.

entries.clue: 10 second abridged Shakespeare? (5)

indicatorNotes.abridged: an abridged book is cut down, so Shakespeare's first name, William, is cut to its short form

blocks.note: s = second
William Shakespeare's first name shortened

annotation.surface: A cheeky review of a condensed Shakespeare: rubbish, like the answer to 10.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 10 across, HOGWASH, which as well as nonsense literally means kitchen scraps fed to pigs.
annotation.definitionFit: A cross-reference: hogwash in its literal sense is pig food, and both words also mean nonsense.

entries.clue: Butcher at the farm? It follows (9)

indicatorNotes.Butcher: to butcher something is to hack it about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Slaughter on a farm, and then what comes after.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' looks like a person, but it is the verb telling you to hack up the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the consequences left behind by an event, usually a bad one.

entries.clue: Meaningless like one three by itself (7)

blocks.note: as = like
I = one, the Roman numeral
three multiplied by itself

annotation.surface: A comment that a lone number three is pointless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By itself' reads as alone, but it means multiplied by itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: literally donkey-like, the word means stupid, with no sense to it.

entries.clue: Get rich from tip put in mug (5,2)

indicatorNotes.put in: one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: a mug is a cup
to tip is to lean; these letters go inside the mug

annotation.surface: A waiter getting rich from the tips dropped in a mug.
annotation.walkthrough: The tip in the surface is money left for service; here it is the verb meaning to tilt.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to make a big profit quickly, as a gambler does after a winning streak.

entries.clue: Creative exploring dreams, possibly making Radio 5 all ads (8,4)

indicatorNotes.possibly: the letters could possibly form something else

blocks.note: taken as written
V = 5, the Roman numeral
taken as written

annotation.surface: A creative type imagining a BBC Radio 5 made entirely of adverts.
annotation.walkthrough: Radio 5 Live is a BBC station that carries no adverts, so the idea is a dream. The 5 is only the Roman numeral V.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the Spanish Surrealist painter built his art from dream imagery.
